Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Time for the main feature: the live game.

A quiz can be played many times (for example, a rehearsal and the real talk). Each time is a new game with its own players and answers. Games skip inactive questions.

The moderator's side:

- The quiz page gets the "Start a game" button. It creates a new game and opens its big-screen page for the moderator (it stays in the moderator area).
- Before the start, the big screen shows the quiz title, the join link as plain text, a QR code with the same link, and the number of players currently waiting for the quiz to start as "Players: 2". The join link is a full URL; the scheme can be left out (for example, `localhost:3000/play/K7RZX`).
- The "Start" button shows the first active question: the progress ("Question 1 of 3"), the question text, and the options. While the question is open, the big screen counts the players who answered as "Answers: 1 / 2" (players who answered / players currently in the game). The second counter is important for moderators 'cause it shows if they need to wait for more answers or not, are there any active players in the game.
- The "Finish" button closes the question. The big screen then shows the number of answers for each option and marks the correct options with "Correct".
- The "Next" button shows the next active question. On the last question, the button is "End quiz" instead, and it ends the game.
- After the end, the big screen shows "The quiz is over".

The player's side:

- A player opens the join link on a phone. No account is needed: the page asks for "Your name" and has the "Join" button. After joining, the player sees "Hi, <name>!" (for example, "Hi, Alice!") and waits for the start.
- The browser remembers the player: opening the join link again in the same browser continues the game as the same player.
- Players can join at any time before the end. After the end, the join link shows "The quiz is over" and does not let anyone join.
- During a question, the player sees the question text and its options as buttons. Tapping an option submits it at once, and the option is marked "Your answer". The player can change the answer until the question is closed; the last pick counts. Players must not be able to find out the correct answer, not even in the page source, before the question is closed.
- After "Finish", the player sees "Correct!", "Wrong!", or "No answer".
- After the end, the player sees "The quiz is over".

Everything is live: the big screen, the counters, and the phones follow the game without page reloads. Participants typically use crowded conference Wi-Fi.

# Quizzy Architecture Notes

## Data Model (Release 1: Moderator Prep)
- `Quiz` (`title`) has_many `Question` ordered by `position, id`.
- `Question` (`quiz_id`, `body`, `position`, `active`) has_many `Option` ordered by `position, id`.
- `Option` (`question_id`, `body`, `correct`, `position`).

## Design & Assets
- Design tokens, layout, and component classes live in `app/assets/stylesheets/quizzy.css` (adapted from `docs/mockups/quizzy.css`) with `app/assets/fonts/Inter-latin.woff2`.
- Lists (`quiz-list`, `question-list`) use semantic `<ul>` / `<li>` items so each item's controls sit inside its `<li>`.
- Confirmation dialogs use `data-turbo-confirm` (native `window.confirm()`).

## Moderator Area & Auth
- Everything under `/moderate` inherits from `Moderate::BaseController` and enforces HTTP Basic Authentication against `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD` using SHA-256 + `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`.
- Preview (`/moderate/quizzes/:id/preview`) is client-side via Stimulus (`preview_controller.js`) over active questions only; no preview answers are persisted.

## Quiz Export & Import
- Export (`GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/export`) serializes `Quiz#export_payload` with `JSON.pretty_generate` inside a single `<pre>` element, writing only `title`, `questions` (`text`, `active`, `options`), and `options` (`text`, `correct`) in preserved order.
- Import (`GET /moderate/quizzes/import`, `POST /moderate/quizzes/import`) is handled by `QuizImport` (`ActiveModel::Model`), validating structure and question/option rules atomically inside a transaction so invalid payloads import nothing. `active` defaults to `true` and `correct` defaults to `false` when omitted.

class QuizImport
  include ActiveModel::Model
  include ActiveModel::Attributes

  attribute :json, :string
  attr_reader :quiz

  def save
    @quiz = nil
    errors.clear

    raw = json.to_s
    if raw.strip.empty?
      errors.add(:base, "Quiz JSON can't be blank")
      return false
    end

    data = parse_json(raw)
    return false unless data

    parsed = validate_payload(data)
    return false unless parsed

    persist_quiz(parsed)
  end

  private

  def parse_json(raw)
    data = JSON.parse(raw)
    unless data.is_a?(Hash)
      errors.add(:base, "Quiz JSON must be a JSON object")
      return nil
    end
    data
  rescue JSON::ParserError => e
    errors.add(:base, "Invalid JSON: #{e.message}")
    nil
  end

  def validate_payload(data)
    title = data["title"]
    if !title.is_a?(String) || title.strip.empty?
      errors.add(:base, "Title can't be blank")
    end

    unless data.key?("questions") && data["questions"].is_a?(Array)
      errors.add(:base, "Questions must be an array")
      return nil

    parsed_questions = data["questions"].each_with_index.filter_map do |q_data, q_idx|

    if options_data.size < 2

    if parsed_options.none? { |o| o[:correct] == true }

For the `current_question`, the approach of finding it by `position` and including options seems right, with `includes(:game_options)` when rendering.

Then, there's `Game#state_version`. I've been thinking about this. The moderator's view is straightforward, a string with the status, question index, player and answer counts, like `#{status}:#{current_question_index}:#{players_count}:#{current_answers_count}`. But the player's view needs to handle the current pick. The initial implementation involves a state version that includes the player ID. It's looking something like this: If the player is nil, its "guest:#{status}" and if there is a player, its "player:#{player.id}:#{status}:#{current_question_index}:#{picked_id || 'none'}".

I have to consider the shared broadcast in `GameBroadcaster.broadcast_question_open(game)`. When a question opens, nobody has answered yet, so `picked_id` is going to be `nil`. The original idea was to broadcast a shared `state_version` and then separately for individual players. I can make the shared broadcast send `{ type: "replace", target: "play-stage", html: html, state_version: "shared:#{game.status}:#{game.current_question_index}:none" }`. This is where I started thinking... The WebSocket already knows the player ID! Why include it in the `state_version` string? I can drastically simplify things.

The state version for the player:  When the player is nil: `"guest:#{status}"`, if the player is there, the state version is `"#{status}:#{current_question_index}:#{picked_id || 'none'}"`! The broadcast and the player's state are now aligned!

This means when a question opens after `Start`/`Next`, all players have a state version `"question_open:0:none"`, and the broadcast also has that state version, `"question_open:0:none"`.

When a player taps an option and their HTTP response updates `#play-stage`, the `data-state-version` updates to something like `"question_open:0:5"`. If they reconnect and `sync`, it's a match, and no-op! And when the moderator clicks `Finish`, the server broadcasts per-picked-option `data-state-version="question_closed:0:5"` (for the player who picked 5) and `"question_closed:0:none"` (for those who didn't pick). For `End quiz`, the server broadcasts `"finished"`.

This is *much* cleaner and simpler.

class Game < ApplicationRecord
  CODE_ALPHABET = "ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789".chars.freeze
  CODE_LENGTH = 5

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :game_questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :players, -> { order(:created_at, :id) }, dependent: :destroy

  enum :status, {
    lobby: "lobby",
    question_open: "question_open",
    question_closed: "question_closed",
    finished: "finished"
  }, validate: true

  validates :code, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :quiz_title, presence: true
  validates :current_question_index, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0 }

  def self.stream_verifier
    Rails.application.message_verifier(:game_stream)
  end

  def self.create_from_quiz(quiz)
    active = quiz.active_questions.includes(:options).to_a
    game = new(quiz: quiz, quiz_title: quiz.title, status: :lobby, current_question_index: 0)

    if active.empty?
      game.errors.add(:base, "Add at least one active question before starting a game")
      return game
    end

    transaction do
      game.code = generate_unique_code
      game.save!

      active.each_with_index do |q, q_idx|
        gq = game.game_questions.create!(
          question: q,
          position: q_idx + 1,
          body: q.body
        )
        q.options.each_with_index do |opt, o_idx|
          gq.game_options.create!(
            option: opt,
            position: o_idx + 1,
            body: opt.body,
            correct: opt.correct?
          )
        end
      end
    end

    game
  end

  def self.generate_unique_code
    loop do
      candidate = Array.new(CODE_LENGTH) { CODE_ALPHABET.sample }.join
      return candidate unless exists?(code: candidate)
    end
  end

  def current_question
    game_questions.includes(:game_options).find_by(position: current_question_index + 1)
  end

  def current_question_number
    current_question_index + 1
  end

  def total_questions
    game_questions.count
  end

  def last_question?
    current_question_index >= total_questions - 1
  end

  def players_count
    players.count
  end

  def current_answers_count
    q = game_questions.find_by(position: current_question_index + 1)
    q ? q.answers.count : 0
  end

  def state_version_for_moderator
    "#{status}:#{current_question_index}:#{players_count}:#{current_answers_count}"
  end

  def state_version_for_player(player)
    return "guest:#{status}" if player.nil?
    return "finished" if finished?
    return "lobby" if lobby?

    q = game_questions.find_by(position: current_question_index + 1)
    picked_id = q&.answers&.find_by(player_id: player.id)&.game_option_id
    "#{status}:#{current_question_index}:#{picked_id || 'none'}"
  end

  def start!
    with_lock do
      return false unless lobby?
      return false if game_questions.empty?

      update!(
        status: :question_open,
        current_question_index: 0,
        started_at: Time.current
      )
      true
    end
  end

  def finish_question!
    with_lock do
      return false unless question_open?

      update!(status: :question_closed)
      true
    end
  end

  def next_question!
    with_lock do
      return false unless question_closed?

      if last_question?
        update!(status: :finished, finished_at: Time.current)
      else
        update!(
          status: :question_open,
          current_question_index: current_question_index + 1
        )
      end
      true
    end
  end

  def join_player(name:)
    with_lock do
      return nil if finished?

      player = players.build(name: name)
      player.save
      player
    end
  end

  def submit_answer!(player:, game_option_id:)
    with_lock do
      return false unless question_open?

      question = current_question
      return false unless question

      option = question.game_options.find_by(id: game_option_id)
      return false unless option

      answer = Answer.find_or_initialize_by(player: player, game_question: question)
      answer.game_option = option
      answer.save!
      true
    end
  end

  def signed_moderator_stream_token
    self.class.stream_verifier.generate({ "role" => "moderator", "game_id" => id })
  end

  def signed_player_stream_token(player)
    self.class.stream_verifier.generate({ "role" => "player", "game_id" => id, "player_id" => player.id })
  end

  def signed_guest_stream_token
    self.class.stream_verifier.generate({ "role" => "guest", "game_id" => id })
  end
end
EOF

class GameChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel
  def subscribed
    payload = Game.stream_verifier.verified(params[:token])
    if payload.blank?
      reject
      return
    end

    @role = payload["role"]
    @game_id = payload["game_id"]
    @player_id = payload["player_id"]

    case @role
    when "moderator"
      stream_from "game:#{@game_id}:moderator"
    when "player"
      stream_from "game:#{@game_id}:players"
      stream_from "game:#{@game_id}:player:#{@player_id}"
    when "guest"
      stream_from "game:#{@game_id}:guests"
    else
      reject
    end
  end

  def sync(data)
    game = Game.find_by(id: @game_id)
    return unless game

    client_version = data["state_version"].to_s

    case @role
    when "moderator"
      server_version = game.state_version_for_moderator
      return if client_version == server_version

      if game.lobby?
        transmit({
          type: "counts",
          players_count: game.players_count,
          answers_count: 0,
          state_version: server_version
        })
      else
        transmit({
          type: "replace",
          html: GameBroadcaster.render_moderator_stage(game),
          state_version: server_version

    when "player"
      player = game.players.find_by(id: @player_id)

class PlayController < ApplicationController
  before_action :set_game
  before_action :load_player

  def show
    assign_stage_variables
  end

  def join
    if @game.finished?
      redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
      return
    end

    if @player
      redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
      return
    end

    new_player = @game.join_player(name: params.dig(:player, :name))
    if new_player.nil?
      redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
    elsif new_player.persisted?
      cookies.signed[player_cookie_name(@game)] = {
        value: new_player.token,
        expires: 7.days.from_now,
        httponly: true,
        same_site: :lax
      }
      GameBroadcaster.broadcast_counts(@game)
      redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
    else
      @player_errors = new_player.errors.full_messages
      @entered_name = params.dig(:player, :name)
      assign_stage_variables
      render :show, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end
  end

  def answer
    if @player.nil?
      redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
      return
    end

    if @game.submit_answer!(player: @player, game_option_id: params[:game_option_id])
      GameBroadcaster.broadcast_counts(@game)
    end

    @game.reload
    assign_stage_variables

    respond_to do |format|
      format.turbo_stream do
        render turbo_stream: turbo_stream.replace(
          "play-stage",
          partial: "play/stage",
          locals: {
            game: @game,
            player: @player,
            question: @question,
            picked_option_id: @picked_option_id,
            state_version: @game.state_version_for_player(@player)
          }
        )
      end
      format.html { redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other }
    end
  end

  def state
    server_version = @game.state_version_for_player(@player)
    if params[:state_version].to_s == server_version || (@player.nil? && !@game.finished?)
      render json: { changed: false }
      return
    end

    assign_stage_variables
    html = render_to_string(
      partial: "play/stage",
      locals: {
        game: @game,
        player: @player,
        question: @question,
        picked_option_id: @picked_option_id,
        state_version: server_version
      }
    )

    render json: {
      changed: true,
      type: "replace",
      html: html,
      state_version: server_version
    }
  end

  private

  def set_game
    code = params[:code].to_s.strip.upcase
    @game = Game.find_by(code: code)
    render :not_found, status: :not_found unless @game
  end

  def load_player
    return unless @game

    token = cookies.signed[player_cookie_name(@game)]
    @player = token.present? ? @game.players.find_by(token: token) : nil
  end

  def player_cookie_name(game)
    "quizzy_player_#{game.code}"
  end

  def assign_stage_variables
    @question = (@game.question_open? || @game.question_closed?) ? @game.current_question : nil
    @picked_option_id = if @player && @question
                          @question.answers.find_by(player_id: @player.id)&.game_option_id
                        end
  end
end

- Player flow lives at `/play/:code` (`PlayController`) and never renders `correct` / `is-correct` in HTML or ActionCable payloads while a question is open.
- Live updates use `GameChannel` (authorized via signed `ActiveSupport::MessageVerifier` tokens) and `GameBroadcaster` (`async` adapter in `config/cable.yml`), paired with `live_screen_controller.js` / `live_play_controller.js` that sync state on WebSocket connect/reconnect/`visibilitychange`/`online` and fall back to `/state` JSON polling if WebSocket is disconnected on flaky conference Wi-Fi.
